legend: The patient is a 13-year-old boy with clinical and laboratory findings consistent with Cushing disease. MRI showed a 4 mm lesion in the left lateral wing and cavernous sinus invasion. The surgical specimen showed a corticotroph adenoma/tumour with extensive immunoreaction for ACTH.

The patient is a 13-year-old boy with clinical and laboratory findings consistent with Cushing disease. MRI showed a 4 mm lesion in the left lateral wing and cavernous sinus invasion. The surgical specimen showed a corticotroph adenoma/tumour with focal areas of incomplete acini disruption suggestive of hyperplasia (reticulin silver).

diagnosis: Growth hormone–secreting tumour associated with X-linked acrogigantism
legend: A 5-year-old girl referred for treatment of gigantism. The patient’s paediatrician noted consistent elevation of her growth rate after the age of 30 months when she was at the 90th percentile for height. Her weight percentile increased over this time as well, and at the time of surgery at the age of 5 years, she was the height of an average 8-year-old (50th percentile for 8 years). Laboratory tests revealed a growth hormone level of 85.4 ng/mL and an IGF1 level of 806 ng/mL. MRI showed a pituitary macroadenoma with chiasmal compression. Genetic analysis demonstrated a germline GPR101 duplication consistent with X-linked acrogigantism {27245663}. Most patients with X-linked acrogigantism develop growth hormone–secreting tumours, but somatotroph hyperplasia may also be seen. In this patient, a mixed somatotroph and lactotroph adenoma/tumour was present. Here, a dual population of cells can be seen, with large, densely granulated cells (upper right) next to smaller, sparsely granulated cells with slight eosinophilic cytoplasm (lower left).

diagnosis: Growth hormone–secreting tumour associated with familial isolated pituitary adenoma
legend: Non-identical twin girls presented as adolescents to the emergency department with severe progressive headache caused by large pituitary macroadenomas requiring emergency neurosurgery. Both patients were found to have silent somatotroph adenomas/tumours on pathological examination (not shown). Furthermore, the light microscopic, immunohistochemical, and electron microscopic studies demonstrated tumours of virtually identical characteristics. The adenomas were accompanied by multiple areas of somatotroph hyperplasia (shown here and Fig. <<#18162>>). Genetic analyses revealed a novel E216X mutation of the AIP gene, which was present both in the affected patients and in their unaffected father {21450940}. Here, reticulin silver histochemical stain shows expansion of the acini but maintenance of the regular reticulin network of normal adenohypophysis.

legend: Lactotroph adenoma/tumour. An 11-year-old girl was referred to the pituitary clinic after a pituitary tumour was found incidentally on MRI, which was performed on account of severe persistent headaches. Visual field testing revealed a dense hemianopsia on the right, and inferior temporal loss on the left. Laboratory tests revealed a prolactin level of 433 ng/mL and normal growth hormone, IGF1, free thyroxine (T4), and TSH levels. She was started on cabergoline, with significant reduction in her prolactin level. However, there was little reduction of the tumour size, and the patient continued having persistent headaches and visual deficits. A surgical resection was performed. Postcontrast T1-weighted coronal MRI showing a heterogeneously enhancing large pituitary tumour (18.8 × 17.6 mm) occupying the sella and suprasellar extension that abuts the chiasm eccentric to the left, with slight signal abnormality of the chiasm.

legend: A minority of patients with acromegaly may have a mixed gangliocytoma–somatotroph adenoma/tumour. The two cellular elements can be seen intermixed or in isolated areas. Ganglionic cells vary in shape and size, some with dense Nissl substance, and they are commonly embedded in a neuropil-like matrix.

Invasive adenoma/tumour. T1-weighted postcontrast coronal MRI demonstrates a very large heterogeneously enhancing tumour centred in the sellar region with suprasellar and parasellar extension and invasion of the sphenoid sinus and clivus. Both internal carotid arteries are completely encased.

legend: Irrespective of their subtypes, these tumours are positive for TPIT.

diagnosis: Densely and sparsely granulated corticotroph adenomas/tumours
legend: Irrespective of their subtypes, these tumours tend to display diffuse cytoplasmic reactivity for low-molecular-weight cytokeratin (CAM5.2).

This tumour from a patient with hyperthyroidism is composed of pale acidophilic cells with variable morphology, including polygonal cells that resemble thyrotrophs. They have prominent nuclear inclusions that resemble irregular nucleoli (inset); these have been called spheridia. This tumour expressed nuclear PIT1 with variable growth hormone (GH) and TSH but no prolactin (PRL); there is diffuse α-subunit (αSU) positivity. Tumours of this lineage have variable positivity for the three PIT1-lineage hormones.

diagnosis: Multiple synchronous pituitary adenomas / pituitary neuroendocrine tumours (PitNETs)
legend: These pituitary adenomas / PitNETs occur in about 1% of patients. In this example, a densely granulated somatotroph tumour stains for PIT1 and growth hormone (GH) and shows diffuse cytoplasmic CAM5.2 reactivity. It traps a small gonadotroph tumour that stains for SF1 and is negative for the other biomarkers examined. Tumours like this one and the common occurrence of trapped non-tumorous tissue may explain why SF1 expression is detected in some tumours causing acromegaly.

title: Diagnostic criteria for pituitary adenoma / pituitary neuroendocrine tumour (PitNET)
tablehtml:
Essential:

Sellar or suprasellar location

AND

Histological features of a low-grade neuroendocrine tumour that displays destruction of the normal anterior gland acinar structure

AND

Subclassification based on immunoreactivity for pituitary hormones and/or lineage-specific transcription factors

Desirable:

Reticulin fibre disruption

Low-molecular-weight cytokeratins, in particular for somatotroph and corticotroph tumours

Tumour proliferation as indicated by either mitotic count or Ki-67 (MIB1) expression
